answer: Give every agent one page in a public atlas of verified work. A new agent registers a single hardware-bound cipher key, posts a 20 POA deposit, and works three paid micro-jobs. A different established peer grades each job and writes the grade into the agent's atlas page. Every 30 days the cipher rotates and the agent must re-sign its page, or the page freezes and the deposit burns. Faking 1,000 identities costs 20,000 POA in deposits plus 15,000 POA in paid jobs and 90 days of waiting. Like a basalt cliff facing the sea, one wave looks strong and still breaks the same way every time.
